Moczydly Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Raczki, Poland

Not demolished. Jews are first recorded in Raczki in 1670, reaching 55.6% (1,464) of the population by 1911 before declining to 22.4% (413) by 1938, with most murdered during WWII. This cemetery, confirmed by cartographic sources (including an 1795-1805 military map) to exist no later than 1805, fell into disrepair during and after the war; Poland formally closed it in 1964. A 1991 provincial survey found a poorly maintained metal-mesh fence and no visible traces of graves, recommending cleanup and an information board. A planned 2013 bypass road through part of the cemetery was ultimately rerouted after officials reconsidered.
